s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic, progressive, asymptomatic, localized skin and hair lesion with scarring alopecia
salient_findings: Arc-shaped, depressed skin groove on the left side of the forehead, frontal scalp, and vertex area
Localized linear hair loss and hair thinning on the left scalp area
Presence of short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation on dermoscopic examination
key_facts: The patient is a man in his 50s
The lesion began approximately 10 years earlier
The patient received 2 doses of intralesional steroid via injection on a small bald patch on the vertex
The lesion gradually progressed to the frontal scalp and eventually made a linear furrow on the left side of his forehead
The patient denied any trauma history
The patient had no history of connective tissue disease
No evidence of systemic involvement, such as arthralgia, photosensitivity, or skin rashes
Dermoscopic examination revealed several short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation
The result of a hair pull test was negative
Histopathologic examination showed predominant lymphocytic infiltrates in perifollicular and periappendageal regions of the dermis and lobular panniculitis
Direct immunofluorescence was positive with granular deposition of IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q, and fibrinogen in the dermal blood vessels

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of an asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin groove on the forehead, frontal scalp, and vertex area with localized linear hair loss and hair thinning, along with dermoscopic findings of short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation, is consistent with frontal fibrosing alopecia. The absence of systemic involvement and negative antinuclear antibody test also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: lupus panniculitis
rejected.why: The patient had no history of connective tissue disease and negative antinuclear antibody test, making lupus panniculitis less likely.

rejected.label: linear scleroderma
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and histopathologic examination do not show typical features of linear scleroderma, such as bound-down skin or significant fibrosis.

rejected.label: lichen planopilaris
rejected.why: The patient's dermoscopic findings and histopathologic examination do not show typical features of lichen planopilaris, such as broken hairs or significant interface dermatitis.

rejected.label: scarring alopecia
rejected.why: While the patient has scarring alopecia, the specific diagnosis of frontal fibrosing alopecia is more precise and explains the patient's presentation and findings.
